I just want to start by saying that this game was mostly made by 2 people. While I have my gripes with it, when you look at the size of the game, the amount of content it have, the art direction and its (in my opinion) low price, this game is a must buy.

Tombwater is a top-down souls-like metroidvania. You play as a gunslinger without a name, on his way to the town of Tombwater to meet an old friend. But once you'll arrive, you'll quickly realise that something is wrong with the city and its inhabitants.

The gameplay is good. You fight your way in the streets using everything you have : melee weapons, guns, spells, bombs... The amount of weapons and items in the game is very impressive, and allows you to make multiple different builds. You can go full melee, make your guns you main sources of damages, you can be a powerfull sorcerer and one shot everything with a spell, or combine multiple playstyles. You can be overpowered sure, but the game manage to stay fairly balanced in its progression, so most of the game you'll have to use ALL of your equipement to survive. This give this pretty fun gameplay loop of fast, agressive combat, where you can stay on the offensive anywhere on the battlefield.

What i like the most though, it's the art direction of the game. We clearly don't have enough of Weird West games, and this one manage to get everything right : the pixel art, the colors, the environments, the character and enemy design... It's one of the coolest representation of the genrer in video games, up there with Hunt Showdown and BLOODWEST.

The level design is also pretty good. The town of Tombwater and its surroundings, while very reminiscent of Bloodborne's Yharnam, still conserve its own identity, and despite being essentially made of corridors, platforming sections and arenas, Tombwater still manage to feel like a "real" city. Exploration is well rewarded, as the game is full of hidden chests with useful loot, side-areas and shortcuts to other zones in the city.

Okay I have been prasing the game so far, but what about my "gripes"? Well let's start by how the game can be limiting. I understand that it's probably a game engine issue, but only being able to attack in 4 directions can be frustrating. Combine it with how sensitive the character is to switching directions and multiple times i find myself attacking or using a spell in the wrong direction.

The other limits i'm talking about is how many weapons, spells and items you can equip. While I think 3 for melee weapons and guns is fine, only 3 for spells/tools and consumables is for me a little too limiting. I understand that it's for balancing issues, but there's so many cools spells and items to use... Let's not forget that you main source of healing, the flask, take 1 emplacement. Yes you can play without it, but come on. Let's put it this way : can you imagine how annoying it would be if you could only equip 3 spells and 3 items in Elden Ring ?

The hitboxes aren't that great. Some ennemies and bosses have attacks that feels like it shouldn't hit, and you also have attacks that feels like it shouldn't hit. But the worse might be for platforming : the number of time i had the "falling in the void" animation while i'm on the solid floor/platform is honestly hilarious, but can be frustrating in some more demanding platforming sections.

The level design, that I was praising above, is a double edge sword. The city was really built like a maze, full of narrow streets, multiple layers and buildings that connect everything to each other. It's very easy to get lost in it or to miss entrences to secrets areas, which is fun at first but can really get tedious for the inevitable "go back to places you have been before" of metroidvanias.

Finally, while the game manage to keep a good pace for most of the game, I kinda think that it's too big for its own good. Don't get me wrong I'm impressed by the amount of content of this game, and some of it is optional, but if you want to have the real ending, you'll have to do pretty much everything, and well some of the bonus zones aren't really interesting in terms of content and level design... All that for, in my opinion a pretty lackluster true "boss" and ending. It only slowed the game and made it more tedious for me, and it's awful to say but I kinda recommand going only for the base ending instead.

Anyway, that's pretty much everything I have to say about Tombwater. Don't get theses gripes fools you ; in the end I really enjoyed my time with this game, in fact it was way better than I expected ! If you are longing for a cool spiritual successor to Bloodborne, if you need to scratch that itch of playing an awesome Weird West game, or looking for a new metroidvania to add at your collection, give Tombwater a try : you won't be disappointed.

Tombwater is a fantastic indie take on the soulslike genre that can essentially be summed up as “Bloodborne as a top-down Zelda game in a weird west setting”.

It has the usual hallmarks of a soulslike - bonfires, unlockable shortcuts, corpse runs, doomed NPC quest lines, and obscure lore bits in item descriptions and the like.

It has what you’d expect from a top-down Zelda game - progression based on the acquisition of tools that let you bypass obstacles that were previously impassable, as well as a handful of tools that can aid you in combat.

And the weird west stuff…well. As the Bloodborne influence might imply, this is more weird west by way of Lovecraft etc than what you might see in something like Deadlands, and it works extremely well. There are plenty of worldbuilding hints that nod towards larger ideas without explicitly explaining everything.

Anyway, highly recommend if this style of game is even remotely up your alley.

This is a hidden gem of a game. High praise and recommendations. Played with an xbox controller.

What You Need To Know:
1. It's Bloodborne and Hunt the Night in the weird west.

2. HARD. Fortunately, there are accessibility options so you can tweak damage dealt and received.

3. Your class choice MATTERS. Most of your stats are fixed from the start. You only get more health, stamina, and resistance to madness (spellcasting ability). So choose wisely.

4. Big map, USE MARKERS. You will forget where you saw the thing. Mark campfires, fast travel bells, shops, etc.

5. There are still areas you missed.

Frankly I loved it, and am surprised how much I missed in terms of achievements. At least one is from a binary so you can't get both from one run. The story was great and only added to the gameplay. There are bits of lore in item descriptions and such but no documents or lore dumps. There are some threads that didn't get pulled so there might be more on the horizon for this game.

reviews.review:
a fun and flawed love letter to bloodborne.

great aesthetic, music, and level design. absolutely abysmal map and navigation.

the combat has its moments, but bosses are largely unenjoyable. you'll constantly take damage after getting stuck in melee animations with significant endlag, which would be fine if your attacks didn't just tickle bosses. furthermore, most bosses have ridiculously short endlag on all of their attacks, so boss fights devolve into 1-2 hits, run around until they are open, then hit again. this is acceptable in games with a lot of spectacle, but it falls flat in tombwater.

*edit after beating the entire game:

later charms vastly improve the combat experience from a frustration standpoint, but the core combat mechanics are still flawed. some endgame melee weapons are fun, but the majority are too unwieldy with the janky hitboxes and startup/endlag. spells and guns decide fights.

Some minor things to be aware of:
- Mark your map when you find things, the game does not do this for you automatically. I like this as it keeps a sense of mystery and exploration instead of just knowing you found something important because the map marked it for you.
- You unfortunately cannot respec from your initial class and those stats do not seem to be upgradable (you can respec some of your stats but not the ones you select at class selection). I personally didn't mind this as I plan on playing multiple runs to try out different builds, but some might not like this limitation.

[h1]Compact but intense Zelda-Souls set in the Weird West[/h1]
Tombwater is definitely worthy of being in the collection of any soulslike fan. Add in the Link's Awakening like array of navigational tools and the Weird West style setting and you've got a pretty unique game. It's good, but not too long. Getting both endings (and beating all bosses I found) took 23 hours. Still haven't gotten all the weapons/charms/flask shards and so on, it'd be nice if the wiki was a little better kept on that front, but you'll be exploring all over the map with fast travel being a bit of a late game convenience rather than a massive help.

Pros:
-Challenging combat with a lot of damage dealing options
-Bosses being pretty unique with only the first one being a loveletter to Bloodborne's first boss
-Movement options expand with each new tool you get
-Tons of secrets to discover
-Tight controls

Cons:
-Too well hidden secrets and too few clues for a lot of them
-Reaching the actual final boss requires assembling a mcguffin and using it in the battle vs the regular final boss. The game does not explain this
-Some boss/spell/minion combinations can yeet you back to the bonfire almost instantly due to placement and hit registration.
-Money is scarce until you get the charm to change this.

Very good game.

Positives:

- Lots of bosses.
- Huge variety of weapons, spells, and charms to discover.
- Plenty of secrets to find.
- A massive world that's easy to get lost in.
- A fresh take on the Zelda/Soulslike formula.

Negatives:

- The biggest issue is the map. It's honestly just straight up dog sh*t. It's too vague to be reliable, and even using markers doesn't help much because the map doesn'thave any meaningful details. It only gives you a rough idea of where you are within a zone, and even that isn't always accurate. Areas like the sewers connect to multiple regions, and the sub-areas don't have maps at all, this makes it so frustrating.

- My other issue/nitpick is how water and bottomless pits work. The game gives you a short window to get back to solid ground, but sometimes it's simply impossible and you drown anyway. The health loss isn't a big deal, but the respawn is. You're placed right on the edge of the water or pit, so even the slightest movement can send you straight back in. It's especially frustrating when you need to dash, since dashing follows your movement direction and often launches you directly back into the hazard. You have to carefully step away from the edge before you can safely dash.

Despite these issues, Tombwater is absolutely worth playing. The water/pit respawn problem feels like something that could be patched fairly easily. The map, however, really needs a complete rework. If the navigation were improved, this game would be close to perfect.

Overall, this game is really great. It’s a good soulslike metroidvania where exploration and searching are rewarded in ways you don’t expect. It’s full of secrets, bosses, hidden walls, and hidden places. There are lots of weapons, both melee and ranged, but the most enjoyable part for me was the spells. I played as a mage and caused TOTAL annihilation of almost every living creature in one shot, even bosses.

I wish the developers all the best. However, I would like to suggest a few possible improvements:

The map. I understand the idea of exploration, but sometimes it gets really confusing. I think you could make players’ lives easier by adding an option for automatic map markers. Opening the map every time to place markers that are not very informative is insanely boring and frustrating. I’ve even seen people selling their own maps online, which is not okay.
Excellent cowboy themed Zeldaborne. For anyone on the fence after the demo the full game is much better and you are introduced to the excellent soundtrack. Its even on sale atm. Just buy it.
Classic Legend of Zelda Wild western bloodborne like

クリア済。

戦闘は近接・銃・魔法の3系統ですが、近接は攻撃前の溜めが気になり、敵側の機動力や連続攻撃も激しいため、銃主体のヒット＆アウェイ気味な立ち回りになりがちでした。
一方で銃はかなり強く、近接で弾を補充しながら戦う流れは良かったです。魔法も強力なものはあるのですが、装備枠が少なくやや扱いづらめ。

探索面はマップが抽象的で少し見づらく、導線も弱め。
ファストトラベルもありますが、有料解禁かつ利便性はそこまで高くありません。とはいえ、昔の見下ろし型アクションRPGっぽい迷いやすさとして楽しめる部分もありました。

気になったのは、全体的にやや単調なところ。
武器種や敵パターン、防御手段の幅があまり広くなく、ビルドや周回で大きく遊び方が変わる感じではありません。

ボリュームはしっかりあり、価格分は十分楽しめました。
惜しい部分はありつつも、雰囲気込みで楽しめる作品だったと思います。
Just buy it. Simple.

Pretty decent game. Some points for buyers:

* This is more of a zelda/hollowknight-like than a souls-like. You get great exploration and mood. The combat system is interesting, but quite a few steps away from an actual souls game.
* The characters are neat, decent enough mood/story and quests
* Some of the bosses are fun, but overal not super-impressed, more bullet-hell or zelda/hollowknight style bosses
* Bit of a maze, missing a good map, expect lots of backtracking. Can be a bit frustrating
* Leveling up is uninteresting, only 3 stats to choose from, most of the power-boosts are gotten from items (embers). 

If you're expecting a 2d-soulslike, this might not be the game for you. There are some souls-like aspects (dash, stamina, refillable potions), but it's not that. It's the most fun when exploring its interesting map and secrets, but you might want to wait to see if it's going to get a decent overview map added to the game. Exploration is peak, combat and bosses are decent enough, with a fun enough story and a moody atmosphere.

I really, really want to like this game but I've been having a load of problems that keep compounding throughout my time playing. My biggest gripe is the melee. Aiming your gun feels great, its omnidirectional and dodging between shots and firing back feels really cool. At first I thought I would enjoy the idea of using melee to recharge your gun, and in the first few fights it worked out seemlessly. However, that quickly changes when you have to dodge faster enemies or ones that attack in wide arcs. I then quickly realized that for some godforsaken reason, your melee attacks are locked to only swing up and down or left and right in an incredibly small arc or with a lunge that usually just runs you into an enemies attack unless you bait them to swing first (which only works if you bait out their slowest attack most of the time, and even then sometimes you'll just end up behind them and get hit anyway if you're using a lunging weapon). Enemies either attack at an almost instant speed or patiently wait for you to blow them to pieces with a shotgun. Sometimes they stagger when you hit them. Sometimes they don't. Sometimes it feels like bosses stagger far more easily than any of the normal enemies.

Spells feel like a necessity with the strange melee combat because they just circumvent it for the most part, but when you have particularly long engagements you're forced back into melee. Also you can't animation cancel most of your melee attacks, even with the fast hitting ones, so you're just going to face tank a bunch of hits unless you get lucky and an enemy consistently uses their slowest attacks. It seems like the optimal strategy is to get an enemy in a weird spot and use spells that consistently deal damage or poke them with long melee attacks, and there are unfortunately a LOT of spots where enemies get stuck and just let themselves get wailed on.

All of this would be fine if the combat were slower to mix into this if this were a more methodical game, but later bosses especially are essentially bullet hells where you have to dodge constantly only pausing to get a shot or two in before continuing to dodge again. This would also be fine if melee didn't have this many problems.

There are also a TON of instances I encountered where I would kill an enemy while it is in mid-attack animation, only for its attack to still deal damage without any animation playing. This is made doubly worse from your character's MASSIVE hitbox, making projectiles and attack ranges incredibly deceptive since enemy animations don't match up with their effective radius. I found myself constantly getting hit by attacks that seemed incredibly faraway, or falling off cliffs and traps despite my character still being on the ledge or away from spikes. 

This game is frustrating in that it has a lot of potential, but it feels held back by a lot of really small problems that have honestly tarnished my experience playing it.

I'm going to try and finish it because I enjoy a lot of games similar to this (i.e. Bloodborne and Enter the Gungeon), but I hate to say that I can't recommend Tombwater in its current state.

EDIT: So, I finished the game and went back to collect everything I needed for the True Ending as well but I think it didn't really change my opinion much unfortunately.
